title: Function Review: Swiss Army Knife
story: You've been building one tool at a time — a math function here, a string function there. Now it's time to open the whole toolbox and see everything you can build with functions. Your toolkit is growing fast!
why: Functions are the building blocks of every program. This review cements all the patterns you've learned — math, strings, booleans, conditionals, and random — into one cohesive toolkit.
analogy: Your function toolkit is like a Swiss Army knife — each blade does one job, but together they can handle almost anything. The more functions you build, the more capable your toolkit becomes.
try_it: Add one more function of your OWN design — something you wish existed. A tip calculator? A password strength checker? A number guessing game? Build it using everything you know!
tips: A great function does ONE thing and does it well — name it for what it does
Functions can call other functions — build small pieces, then combine them
Every `if/elif/else`, every formula, every string transform can be wrapped in a reusable function
common_mistakes: Trying to put everything in main — main should be short, delegating work to functions
Writing a function that does too many things — "calculate_and_print_and_save" should be three functions
Avoiding function calls because 'it's just one line' — even one-line functions add clarity and reusability
